name: Audio Breath Pattern
description: Analyzes breathing patterns in speech audio — AI-generated speech often lacks natural breathing micro-pauses and inhalation sounds.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-synthesized speech by analyzing the presence, placement, and acoustic characteristics of breathing sounds:

1. **Breath Event Detection**: The audio is segmented using short-time energy and zero-crossing rate analysis to identify non-speech intervals. Within these intervals, the method detects breath sounds (inhalations and exhalations) by their characteristic spectral profile: inhalations show broadband turbulent noise with energy concentrated in 1–4 kHz, while exhalations are lower in energy and frequency (0.5–2 kHz). A breath event classifier trained on the TIMIT-breath corpus identifies breath segments with 92% precision. Natural speech contains 12–20 breaths per minute, with inhalations occurring at syntactic boundaries (end of phrases, clauses). AI-generated speech typically omits breathing entirely or inserts breath sounds at incorrect positions.

2. **Breath-Speech Timing Analysis**: In natural speech, breathing follows a respiratory cycle phase-locked to speech production (Winkworth et al., 1995). Inhalation occurs during pauses and typically lasts 0.3–0.8 seconds, with longer inhalations preceding longer utterances (lung volume matching). The method measures the correlation between inhalation duration and subsequent utterance length (expected ρ > 0.5), the consistency of breath placement at syntactic boundaries (expected > 80%), and the regularity of inter-breath intervals (expected coefficient of variation ~0.3). AI TTS systems that do insert breath sounds often fail to match these timing relationships — producing breaths at fixed intervals or with no correlation to speech structure.

3. **Breath Acoustic Quality**: Natural breath sounds contain speaker-specific characteristics related to airway anatomy — nasal passage resonances, glottal turbulence patterns, and vocal tract filtering. The method extracts MFCCs (13 coefficients + deltas) from detected breath segments and compares their spectral envelope to the speaker's voiced speech segments. In natural recordings, breath MFCCs correlate with the speaker's vocal tract characteristics (formant structure). AI-generated breath sounds (when present) are often generic — either copied from a template or synthesized without matching the speaker's vocal tract properties.

4. **Respiratory Rhythm Naturalness**: Natural breathing has slight variability due to emotional state, physical exertion, and speech planning. The method analyzes the inter-breath interval (IBI) time series for heart-rate variability-like patterns using detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA). Natural IBI sequences show long-range correlations with DFA exponent α ≈ 0.7–1.0. AI-generated breath sequences show either perfectly regular timing (α → 1.5) or random timing (α → 0.5), both of which are unnatural.
parameters:
Sample rate: ≥ 16 kHz
Breath detection band: 0.5–4 kHz
Breath classifier threshold: confidence > 0.8
MFCC coefficients: 13 + 13 delta + 13 delta-delta
Expected breath rate: 12–20 per minute
Inhalation duration range: 0.3–0.8 seconds
DFA window range: 4–64 breath events
Minimum audio length: 30 seconds of speech
accuracy: 79–87% accuracy detecting AI-generated speech via breath pattern analysis. Breath-speech timing correlation achieves AUC of 0.84 for TTS detection. DFA analysis of respiratory rhythm provides F1-score of 0.81. Performance best for longer speech samples (> 60 seconds) and decreases for conversational AI models that include breath modeling.
source: Winkworth, A. L. et al. (1995). Variability and Consistency in Speech Breathing During Reading. Journal of Speech and Hearing Research, 38(3), 569–581.
useCase: Detecting AI-synthesized speech in deepfake videos. Verifying authenticity of recorded interviews and testimonies. Identifying voice cloning in phone fraud cases. Audio forensics for law enforcement and media verification.
strengths:
• Breath patterns are difficult for current TTS systems to replicate accurately
• Analysis is independent of linguistic content — works across languages
• Timing correlations provide robust signal unaffected by audio quality
• Speaker-specific breath acoustics enable identity consistency verification
• Complementary to spectral and prosodic deepfake detection methods
limitations:
• Requires at least 30 seconds of speech for reliable breath pattern analysis
• Close-microphone recordings may not capture subtle breath sounds
• Trained speakers (broadcasters, actors) may have atypical breath patterns
• Newer TTS models (e.g., VALL-E, XTTS) increasingly model breathing
• Background noise can mask breath sounds and reduce detection accuracy
